issues.note: The pair is shaky, since 'also is' occurs with stress; the real fault is the note.
Plain, accurate phrasal definition; objection is taste.
Note already hedges with 'usually'; final position for too/as well is the norm.
The correction agrees with 'She is also a teacher'; only the questionable error pair is real.
Hedged 'often' is true; formal style commonly prefers 'in addition'.
'Also my sister came' is not idiomatic; additive focus is covered by sense 1.
The note says before be; its own correction puts also after be.
Unnatural placement; should be 'Kim also wants to come.'
'Fixed place' overstates, and the note repeats the synonym-discrimination placement rule.
Same unnatural word-order example; unsafe for a learner to copy.
Similarly adds a parallel point, but it is a weak confusable.

findings.F1: Learner-error note says also comes before be, contradicting its own correction 'She is also a doctor'.
findings.F2: Example 'Kim wants also to come.' has unnatural word order for American English.
findings.F3: Adaptation grammar note calls also's position fixed and restates the placement rule already in synonym_discrimination.
